title: Package loader, instances, compression
summary: This is one of the best-engineered corners of the kernel. The v3 model is right for an 8088: a package owns a segment at org 0, so the file is the image. Everything good here follows from it: a header fence shared with the driver loader, a re-check after the full read, in-place decompression with no margin and no second buffer, a re-home that is a base move, and teardown by owner stamp and W_SEG sweep rather than by trusting the package. That attribution is better than Win16 or AmigaOS ever managed. The weaknesses all have one shape. The hostile-input discipline the code advertises has three holes on the COMPRESSED path. The worst is an image shorter than its own clear prefix: the expected-output length wraps, and the decoder writes ~64KB past the region. Several rules about the loader's own state are held by prose, not by a compare: no nested start, UI task only, BX is a window, and [ld_said] is always consumed. All of these can be closed with no ABI break for tens of resident bytes. The documentation is the weakest part. SPEC 21 and 29, and several code banners, still describe things that are gone: the v2 pool, the KB granule, region freeing by the record store, a task word in the kind table, an icon table, and BX sanity checks. (Verified: all five bug findings and both hazards confirmed against the code; the API-level proposal corrected, since os88pkg.py already keeps header byte 31 zero.)

strengths.title: The file IS the image (v3, org 0, own segment)
strengths.why: No relocation pass, and a header peek is all the validation needs. It is what makes in-place expansion (loader.inc:1009-1083) and the re-home as a base move (:1577-1793, mem_reown_x) possible. The .COM model, with a header DOS never had.

strengths.title: One header prologue for packages and drivers
strengths.why: The version is the only argument, and LD_EVER is the one refusal that says why. Modules stay out on purpose, which keeps SPEC 51.1's two independent gates.

strengths.title: Carry fence and 32-bit size ladder, shared with the re-home arm
strengths.why: image + bss is fenced on the carry. A part's header gets exactly the bounds a file's does, so the two ways of starting a program cannot diverge.

strengths.title: Abort believes nothing the package says
strengths.why: Windows are destroyed by their W_SEG stamp, claims are freed by owner word, and XMS is released. The package's own toast is re-homed so its reason survives. Copy this shape wherever the kernel undoes third-party work.

strengths.title: The entry proc is an identified dispatch
strengths.why: Sound grants, XMS, toasts and the file-API folder raised by an entry proc are attributed to it. A stamp is spent only by the task that wrote it, so attribution is correct under pre-emption.

strengths.title: In-place expansion with a raw tail; both pointers bounded; fast path refuses identically
strengths.why: R = U - P is exactly enough, with one claim and no window, so it works on 128KB. The KHP_LZ inline path makes every refusal the slow path made at the same symbol. This is the template for any future decoder.

strengths.title: Instance table mechanics
strengths.why: There is one pointer-bounded walk. The snapshot record IS the instance record, so the cli window is one rep movsw. Per-instance current directories cost nothing when nothing moved, which beats DOS's machine-global cwd.

strengths.title: New header field adopted with no format bump
strengths.why: The worker stack class rides a byte that was always 0. An out-of-range value gets the largest class instead of a refusal. This is the model for extending the header compatibly.

strengths.title: Compressor is a module that sizes itself to the machine; Uncompress is stricter than the loader
strengths.why: The window drops until the tables fit, so a 128KB machine runs the same encoder over less history. The verb already refuses prefix >= image, which is the check the resident loader lacks (loader-1).

findings.title: Compressed package with image smaller than its clear prefix: decoder writes ~64KB past the region
findings.detail: ld_check_hdr bounds the image only to >= 32 and against the file. The icon rule (image >= 96) is os88pkg's alone. Step 6a computes the clear prefix from the flags (up to 320 bytes with bits 0, 1, 5 and 7), then does `sub cx, bx` and `sub dx, bx` with no carry test. Example: image 64, prefix 320. DX = 0xFF00, so lz_decomp_x must produce 65,280 bytes into base+20 paragraphs of a 512-byte region. One literal plus an LZ4 match at offset 1 floods everything above the region. With top-down placement, that is the last-launched package's code. The file can be under 64 bytes, with the crafted stream in its first sector's slack. SPEC 20.13.8.1 covers only the file-shorter-than-prefix half and wrongly concludes that the output bound keeps writes in the region. The image arm (ld_pkg_start_x -> .expand) has the same hole, and The Wire feeds that arm network bytes. The module's cmz_uncomp already checks this.
evidence: kernel/loader.inc:1066-1067 sub cx,bx / sub dx,bx, no carry test
SPEC.md:49072-49075 claim that the output bound keeps writes inside the region
kernel/compress.inc cmz_uncomp .pkg: cmp dx, bx / jae .rbad (the module does check)
findings.recommendation: Refuse image <= prefix and file <= prefix before the two subtracts, exiting through an LD_EBAD stub that pops the push ds at :1011. Better: compute the prefix once in ld_check_hdr, which already holds the flags in DL. Store it in a .bss word and test image > prefix, file > prefix and the loader-3 region fit there, where a refusal owes no unreserve. Step 6a then reads the word.
findings.bytes_est: +14 .cold resident standalone; ~+18 .cold for loader-1 and loader-3 together (ESTIMATED)
findings.prior_art: Mac System 7's dcmp resource decompressors bounded output to the resource's declared size, not to a size derived from untrusted header arithmetic.
findings.verify_note: Re-read: ld_check_hdr's .over arm asks only image > file and image >= 32; step 6a's `sub dx, bx` (image - prefix) has no carry test, and lz_decomp_x's only write bound is that count (lz_take on LZ_F_REM). Image 64 + flags icon|assoc|glyph|card|compressed gives DX = 0xFF00. Same path on the image arm (jmp ld_run_body_x.expand). Not in ABI-BREAK-LIST or KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE; SPEC 20.13.8.1 wrongly says the output bound holds (doc fix supplied). The project's own threat model (SPEC 19, lz.inc 'BOTH ARE BOUNDS-CHECKED AND THAT IS NOT OPTIONAL') is what makes this high: a package is code once it runs, so the realistic trigger is a corrupt or foreign file, turned into memory corruption instead of 'Bad package'. Byte estimate plausible (two cmp/jbe pairs plus a pop-ds stub).

findings.title: Disk-swap re-check does not bound the new header's image+bss against the region
findings.detail: The step 6a re-check rewrites [ld_img], [ld_bss] and [ld_ent] from the in-region header. [ld_need] was sized from the peek's values. Plain packages keep image == file, but bss is unconstrained, and on the parts and compressed arms the image is too. A header that changed between peek and read (a swapped floppy, or a redirected-volume host file rewritten between FSV_READAT and the full read) makes step 7's rep stosb zero past the region. The image arm has the same time-of-check gap against the caller's buffer.
evidence: kernel/loader.inc:1167-1175 need sized from the peek
kernel/loader.inc:1303-1307 bss zero uses the re-checked values
findings.recommendation: After the re-check, add `cmp dx, [ld_need] / ja` to an LD_EBAD exit. DX already holds image + bss from ld_hdr_size.
findings.verify_note: Re-read: the re-check at .expanded rewrites [ld_img]/[ld_bss]/[ld_ent]; for a plain image the ladder forces image == [ld_fsz] (unchanged) but bss is free, so step 7's rep stosb uses a bss [ld_need] never sized. DX = image+bss does survive ld_check_hdr (only AL and CL are written after ld_hdr_size). +6 is right: `cmp dx, [ld_need]` is 4 bytes and `ja` 2, aimed at the existing `mov al, LD_EBAD` just above .ret2j (it needs a label).

findings.title: Compressed read/copy can overrun the region by up to 512 bytes
findings.detail: ld_where places a compressed file at R = roundup512(image - file). Step 6 reads roundup512(file) bytes there, and the image arm copies file bytes. The two round-ups together can exceed roundup512(image+bss) by 512 when bss is short. os88pkg.py and the module's cmz_hdr refuse such files; the kernel does not. The loader's own comment says 'this cannot overflow it'.
evidence: SPEC.md 20.13.8.1 names the guard, not taken
findings.recommendation: Add R + file <= roundup512(image + bss) in ld_check_hdr's .over arm. This equals the round-up form because R is a multiple of 512. Fold it with loader-1.
findings.bytes_est: ~+16 .cold standalone; see loader-1 for the combined figure (ESTIMATED)
findings.verify_note: Re-read ld_where and cmz_hdr: the kernel never asks R + roundup512(file) <= roundup512(image + bss). Up to 512 on the disk read is right (SPEC 20.13.8.1's own example reaches 1,536 in 1,024, though its prose says 511 - doc fix supplied); the image arm's copy of `file` bytes overruns by at most 511. The recommendation's equivalence holds because R and need are both multiples of 512.

findings.title: Entry proc's returned BX is not validated on success
findings.detail: On CF=0, step 9 passes BX straight to the WF_DESK test, inst_bind_win and wm_show. Inside inst_bind_win, wm_ptr2idx's div cl raises INT 0 once BX - wm_wins exceeds 255*WIN_SIZE, and BX=0 is that case. On an 8088 the BIOS dummy handler returns past the div with garbage, the clamp maps it onto the last window, and this record steals that window's wm_owner. On a 286 running kern_big the fault returns to the div and the machine hangs. SPEC 21 step 9 claims BX is sanity-checked; that text describes the retired abort path. inst_wchk needs an owner, which an unpublished record lacks.
findings.recommendation: At .reg, check that BX - wm_wins < MAX_WIN*WIN_SIZE and that [bx+W_SEG] == [ld_base] (the stamp .sweep already trusts). Otherwise go to .abort, which sweeps whatever the entry made.
findings.verify_note: Re-read .reg: BX goes unchecked to [bx+W_FLAGS+1], inst_bind_win (wm_ptr2idx's div) and wm_show. On kern_big wm_wins = 9FCAh (build/kernel.map), so BX = 0 gives 6036h, past 255*74 = 49B6h: the div faults, and the kernel installs no INT 0 handler. Severity medium stands as a robustness fence (a package is trusted code, but every other package-supplied window pointer goes through inst_wchk). The W_SEG compare must be checked against kern_mega's selector stamps and the re-home arm's new [ld_base] before it lands; realistic cost ~+8 (W_SEG) to ~+18 (with the range test).

findings.title: 'No nested start' and 'UI task only' for OSAPI_PKG_START are prose, not fences
findings.detail: SPEC 21.5.4 says an entry proc may not START a package because ld_start holds the outer launch's state. Only the document arm honours this, by posting. The image arm and the plain by-name arm re-enter the pipeline unconditionally. A nested start overwrites [ld_rec], [ld_base], [ld_need] and [ld_lname], then zeroes [ld_base] at its own step 9. The outer launch then publishes I_SPTR=0 on an already-published record. Neither api_rn nor the body checks [sch_cur], so a worker calling the slot runs the loader concurrently with the UI task.
evidence: kernel/loader.inc:2048-2049 only the doc arm tests [ld_base]
SPEC.md 21.5.4 'An entry proc may not START a package'
findings.recommendation: Add `cmp byte [sch_cur], 0 / jne .bad` at the slot's head. Add `cmp word [ld_base], 0 / jne .bad` on the image arm and on the no-document by-name arm; the document arm keeps its post.
findings.prior_art: Win16 LoadModule was non-reentrant too, and serialised itself with a module-loading semaphore rather than relying on callers.
findings.verify_note: Re-read: only ld_pkg_byname's document arm tests [ld_base]; ld_pkg_start_x's image arm and the `jz ld_run_name_x` no-document arm go straight into the pipeline, and api_rn checks no [sch_cur]. A nested start from an entry proc overwrites [ld_rec]/[ld_base]/[ld_need]; the outer .reg then writes I_SPTR = 0 and binds the outer window onto the inner, already-published record, and the outer region is left owned by an unpublished slot. A worker caller already breaks SPEC 20.6 rule 7 (workers touch no file), so the sch_cur fence is defence in depth. Estimate nearer ~+15..+21 (two 7-byte compare/branch pairs plus a 7-byte sch_cur test).

findings.title: No load-time refusal for a package needing newer cells at the same PKG_FMT
findings.detail: SPEC 20.2.0.1 says the loader still starts a package that calls cells an old kernel lacks, and that a package copied onto an old machine by hand is unfenced. Only The Wire's cell fence guards against it. Apps disks and system disks are separate floppies, so a newer apps disk in an older machine is the ordinary case. PKG_FMT is a major version only; there is no minor.
evidence: kernel/instance.inc:1242 inst_set_name_x takes 15 of the 16 name bytes; tools/os88pkg.py:122-123 already refuses a 16-byte name
findings.recommendation: Add a one-byte API LEVEL in header byte 31 (the name field's 16th byte, which os88pkg.py already keeps 0 by refusing 16-character names), numbered from the Wire's existing cell levels. Compare it <= the kernel's level in ld_check_hdr and refuse with LD_EVER ('Wrong os8088 version'). os88pkg.py writes the level. Old packages carry 0 and pass, so PKG_FMT does not move. Do it now, because it only protects kernels from this point forward.
findings.listed_as: SPEC.md 20.2.0.1 'What it does not cover' (named, no remedy)
findings.prior_art: GEOS geodes record a protocol (major.minor) per imported library and refuse a load whose minor is too new. Win16's NE header has an expected-Windows-version field, with ordinal imports failing at load. OS/2 1.x fails the load naming the missing ordinal.
findings.verify_note: The gap is real (SPEC 20.2.0.1 names it, with no remedy; ld_hdr_ok compares the version for equality only) and is not in ABI-BREAK-LIST. CORRECTION: os88pkg.py already refuses a 16-character name (parse_name: 'name is 16 bytes with no NUL ... max 15 chars'), so byte 31 is 0 in every os88pkg-written package and the tooling half is only writing the level. Check every other reader of the 16-byte name field (mount harvest, Sticky Apps) before reusing byte 31.

findings.title: [ld_said] leaks out of loads nobody reports, silencing the next failure
findings.detail: .abort sets [ld_said] when the aborting entry proc's own toast is up. ld_say_status and ui.inc's Task Manager route consume it. ldf_ld_pkg_start never calls ld_say_status (it reports in CF), and assoc_run_x's hand-on arm skips it on purpose. In both cases the flag stays 1, and the next Disk-window load failure says nothing.
findings.recommendation: Patch: every site that clears [ld_painted] (loader.inc:612, :2091, assoc.inc:1309) clears the adjacent word pair instead (+1 byte each), plus a clear on the TM route. Better shape: return the painted and said flags in AH beside AL = status, and retire both globals and their clears.
findings.verify_note: Re-read: ld_said is set at .abort/.rehtoast and consumed only by ld_say_status and ui.inc's TM route (xchg ah, [ld_said]). ldf_ld_pkg_start never calls ld_say_status, and assoc_run_x's hand-on arm (`cmp byte [assoc_dapp], ASSOC_FLUSH / jb .fwd`) skips it, so the byte survives to silence the next Disk-window failure. ld_status, ld_painted, ld_said are adjacent in .bss, so the word-clear patch works as described.

findings.title: ld_unreserve is a drifted twin of mem_free_rec (it misses the page-floor lift)
findings.detail: ld_unreserve exists only because the record's I_SPTR and I_KIND are unwritten until step 9. It frees the same slot, segment and kern_mega high pair that mem_free_rec_x does. It lacks mem_free_rec_x's lift of an instance's page floor (SPEC 50.6.6.2). So an entry proc that sets a floor and aborts leaves it standing on the UI task's stamp, which affects every later launch's claims.
findings.recommendation: Write I_KIND = KIND_PKG and I_SPTR = [ld_base] at step 5; the record is unpublished, so no walker sees it. Update I_SPTR in ld_hi and the re-home arm. ld_unreserve then becomes desk drop + cw_xm_release_rec + mem_free_rec_x + [ld_base]=0. Step 9's I_SPTR store goes.
findings.verify_note: Re-read: mem_free_rec_x starts with `mov byte [mem_pg_floor], MEM_LVL_TOP`; ld_unreserve has no such store. An entry proc runs on the UI task, so a floor it sets is stamped task 0 and outlives the abort. Low. (Aside, not this finding: mem_free_rec_x lifts the floor unconditionally, whoever set it.) Byte estimates unverified.

findings.title: DESK.DRV stays loaded when a widget launch meets a full instance table
findings.detail: ld_alloc loads DESK.DRV before the record scan. When inst_alloc then fails, `jc .nomem` skips .nodrv's desk_drop_x. Calling desk_drop_x there is not safe as it stands: it clears IF_DESK on [di], and DI is one past the table on that path. The module stays loaded until the next close runs a drop.
findings.recommendation: On the desk arm, refuse before desk_need when the top-down scan finds no free record; it already walks the table.
findings.verify_note: Re-read: desk_need runs before the top-down scan; a full table falls to inst_alloc, whose failure takes `jc .nomem` past .nodrv's desk_drop_x, and inst_alloc leaves DI = inst_tab + INST_MAX*I_RECSZ, so desk_drop_x there would clear a bit one past the table. Low: the module is dropped at the next close.

findings.title: OSAPI_PKG_START's caller image must be pinned across the call; the contract does not say so
findings.detail: ld_pkg_start_x banks the source segment because ld_alloc can compact the heap. Compaction can move that very source if it is a movable claim, and nothing updates the banked copy. The Wire pins its claim correctly; SPEC 21.5 says only 'ANY segment - it is COPIED'.
findings.recommendation: Add one sentence to SPEC 21.5: a movable claim must be pinned across the call, because the loader's region claim may compact the heap.
findings.verify_note: Re-read: [ld_msrc] is banked before ld_alloc, whose mem_claimp_hi_x may compact; nothing relocates the banked segment. The Wire pins (wr_fpin, 'the loader claims the new region with ES:DI in hand'). A SPEC 21.5 sentence is added as a doc fix.

findings.title: Compressor's gamma searches its top bit from bit 15 down
findings.detail: cmz_gamma loops `shr ax, cl` from CL=15 down; on an 8088 that costs 8+4n clocks per step. The coded values are small, so a typical call runs 13-14 steps, ~900-1,000 clocks, before emitting 2-4 bits. At two calls per match and about one match per 8 bytes, that is ~230 of the banner's ~1,600 clocks per byte. cmz_bit (~250 clocks per bit) and the double hash per literal (cmz_probe, then cmz_ins) are next.
evidence: kernel/compress.inc:1159-1240 cmz_probe hashes; :1265-1273 cmz_ins hashes again
findings.recommendation: Search upward (shr ax,1 until zero, counting), and pass the head slot from probe to fill. Take the lzcomp row's MartyPC cycle count once if it decides anything.
findings.bytes_est: ~0 (DISKOPS.DRV module, .modl); 0 resident. ~10-15% of compress time, ESTIMATED
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked cmz_gamma: the top-bit search starts at CL = 15 and counts down with `shr ax, cl`, and the emit loop shifts from scratch for every bit. The clock arithmetic is plausible; module-only, 0 resident.

findings.title: Three clear-prefix ladders; the module's comment points at a routine that does not exist
findings.detail: The ladder is inline in step 6a and repeated in cmz_cpre, and the Sticky Apps first-sector read implies it again. cmz_cpre calls itself 'ld_cpre's own ladder', but there is no ld_cpre. Folding the module copy onto a resident routine would cost resident bytes to save module bytes.
findings.recommendation: Keep two ladders. Name the loader's copy as a routine if loader-1's combined fix moves it into ld_check_hdr, and fix the comment.
findings.verify_note: No ld_cpre exists anywhere in kernel/; compress.inc:3640 and SPEC.md 54854 both name it (doc fixes supplied for both).

findings.title: bss zeroing, image-arm copy and LZ4 literals are byte strings
findings.detail: rep stosb costs 10 clocks/byte and rep movsb 17 on an 8088; the word forms cost 7 and 12.5. A 20KB bss saves ~12 ms per launch against ~400 ms per int 13h. LZ4 literal runs are short, so the split's fixed cost eats most of the gain.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: rep stosb at step 7 and rep movsb in the image-arm copy. Record only.

findings.title: Instances do not share code (each launch is a full image copy and disk read)
findings.detail: DS=CS is the package contract, so code and data share one segment and a second instance reloads everything. Windows 3.x, OS/2 and GEOS share code between instances. Doing that here is a DS!=CS flag day, which is not worth it. The cheap fraction is the disk read. An opt-in 'pure image' bit (spare bits exist in LD_H_CLASS) would let a second launch copy the first instance's region (~0.2 s of rep movsw) instead of reading and decoding the file (seconds on a floppy).
evidence: kernel/instance.inc:2097-2098 class byte bits 6-7 used, 0-5 a small index
findings.recommendation: Record. Measure how often second instances are launched before spending ~25 bytes on the opt-in clone.
findings.bytes_est: ~+25 .cold for the opt-in clone (ESTIMATED); not proposed
findings.prior_art: Win16/OS/2 shared code segments with per-instance DGROUP and MakeProcInstance thunks; Mac System 6/7 avoided it with one instance per app.

findings.title: Launch resolves an INDEX against the poster's cache: considered posting the name, keep the index
findings.detail: By-name resolution is safer against FIELD-NOTES 4's class of bug, but dskw_stat walks directory sectors. The cache arm costs no read in the common case (measured 3 reads/531 ms vs 2/306). On an XT a read is ~400 ms, so the index stays. The only exposure left is the .loud arm after a purged cache.
findings.recommendation: Record so it is not re-derived; no change.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked loader_run_x's comment: the 3 reads / 531 ms against 2 / 306 measurement is there as quoted.

doc_fixes.old_text: LD_ENOMEM   equ 5               ; instance table or pool exhausted
doc_fixes.new_text: LD_ENOMEM   equ 5               ; instance table full, or no heap claim fits
doc_fixes.why: There is no pool: ld_alloc answers LD_ENOMEM when inst_alloc finds no free record or mem_claimp_hi_x refuses the region (loader.inc ld_alloc .nomem/.nodrv).

doc_fixes.old_text:
; The region is freed by the instance record (SPEC.md 29.2 rule 7): mem_free_rec
; releases every claim the slot owns, so the store that frees a record frees
; its region.
doc_fixes.new_text:
; The region goes with the instance record (SPEC.md 29.2 rule 7): both
; teardown sites call mem_free_rec, which releases every claim the slot owns,
; region included, just before the store that frees the record.
doc_fixes.why: app_close_win (instance.inc .noflush: call mem_free_rec, then mov byte [di+I_STATE], 0) and inst_task_die (call mem_free_rec, then jmp task_exit) free the region explicitly; no store frees it.

doc_fixes.old_text: ; Both callers are .cold and so is this (SPEC.md 2.6), so the call is near.
doc_fixes.new_text: ; All three callers are .cold and so is this (SPEC.md 2.6), so the call is near.
doc_fixes.why: ld_hdr_ok is called by ld_check_hdr (loader.inc), drv_check (driver.inc, in .cold) and the re-home arm (loader.inc ld_start .rehome) - the banner above already says 'all three callers'.

doc_fixes.old_text: cmp [es:si+LD_H_VER], al                 ; 6 = package, 7 = driver: the
doc_fixes.new_text: cmp [es:si+LD_H_VER], al                 ; PKG_FMT = package, DRV_VER = driver: the
doc_fixes.why: The version bytes are PKG_FMT equ 10 (loader.inc) and DRV_VER equ 12 (driver.inc), not 6 and 7.

doc_fixes.old_text: ; loader_run - load, relocate and launch the package at a directory index
doc_fixes.new_text: ; loader_run - load and launch the package at a directory index
doc_fixes.why: v3 has no relocation (loader.inc banner: 'v3 HAS NO RELOCATION AT ALL').

doc_fixes.old_text:
; in:  AX = directory index
; out: AL = LD_* status
;
; Steps (SPEC.md 21): validate the dir entry; peek the header via a
; 1-sector read into dsk_secbuf; size the allocation
; (roundup512(max(img+bss, fsize)) - sector granularity means the full-file
; read can never touch a neighbouring region); reserve an instance record +
; pool region; read the whole file; re-check the header (disk-swap guard);
; apply the reloc table; zero the bss (killing the table); call the entry;
; register + publish the instance and wm_show its window. Every failure
; path leaves running instances untouched - the reserved record was never
; published, so it (and with it the region) is simply still free.
doc_fixes.new_text:
; in:  SI -> the staged directory entry (loader_run_x stages it)
; out: AL = LD_* status
;
; Steps (SPEC.md 21): the entry's type and size (ld_take); peek the first
; sector (dsk_peek_x) and validate the header where it landed; size and
; reserve the record and its region, roundup512(img + bss) (ld_alloc); read
; the image - or the compressed file, high in the region - and expand it;
; re-check the header in the region (disk-swap guard); then ld_start: zero
; the bss, call the entry, register + publish the instance and wm_show its
; window. Every failure path leaves running instances untouched: the
; reserved record was never published, and ld_unreserve gives the region
; back.
doc_fixes.why: ld_run_body_x reads [si+LD_DE_TYPE] (SI, not AX), peeks with dsk_peek_x, sizes need = roundup512(img+bss) in ld_alloc, has no pool and no reloc table, and frees the claimed region through ld_unreserve (.ret2).

doc_fixes.old_text:
; LOW_SEG, so the sector lands there and only the 32 header bytes are
    ; staged back into the kernel segment for ld_check_hdr to read.
doc_fixes.new_text:
; LOW_SEG, so the sector lands there and is validated where it landed:
    ; ld_check_hdr reads it through ES.
doc_fixes.why: Step 3 does `mov si, bx / call ld_check_hdr` on ES = LOW_SEG; nothing is staged (its own comment at .hdr says so).

doc_fixes.old_text: ; and this cannot overflow it.
doc_fixes.new_text:
; and this cannot overflow it FOR A FILE os88pkg.py WROTE: a foreign
    ; header can, by up to 512 bytes, and nothing here refuses it (SPEC.md
    ; 20.13.8.1).
doc_fixes.why: ld_check_hdr never tests R + file against roundup512(image + bss); image 1,000, file 600, bss 0 reads to 1,536 in a 1,024-byte region (SPEC.md 20.13.8.1's own example).

doc_fixes.old_text:
; Manager names tasks through it, and the package-region allocator derives
; occupancy from it.
doc_fixes.new_text:
; Manager names tasks through it. (A package region is a heap claim owned by
; its record's slot, SPEC.md 20.1/50.3 - nothing derives occupancy from here.)
doc_fixes.why: ld_alloc claims the region with mem_claimp_hi_x under the record's slot (loader.inc step 5); no allocator walks inst_tab.

doc_fixes.old_text:
